_comment: Canonical Distributed Proofreaders / Project Gutenberg compat macros, shared by ratex (Rust), ManyMath (Dart) and math-games (Python). name: control word without backslash. arity: number of braced arguments. expansion: KaTeX-compatible body with #1..#arity. plain: optional body used by text-only normalizers instead of expansion. category: math | prose | editorial. optional: a [..] group may precede the arguments and is dropped by normalizers. ratex: false if ratex cannot register it as a text macro. source/justification: where the corpus preamble defines it. Regenerate ManyMath's compat_macros.g.dart after editing.

macros.name: ds
macros.justification: \newcommand{\ds}{\displaystyle}

macros.name: efrac
macros.justification: \newcommand{\efrac}[2]{\frac{#1}{#2}}: two arguments, passed through to \frac

macros.name: Frac
macros.justification: No corpus preamble defines it; a classical-transcription convention kept for the DP/PG texts.

macros.name: dint
macros.justification: No corpus preamble defines it; a classical-transcription convention kept for the DP/PG texts.

macros.name: sqrtp
macros.justification: Modernize=true (the default): \sqrtp[#1]{#2} is \sqrt[#1]{#2}, i.e. \sqrt's own syntax, so it is an alias that keeps the optional index

macros.name: DELTA
macros.justification: Modernize=false definition. NOTE: the default Modernize=true swaps it to \epsilon (line 342); kept as \delta because the Rust, Dart and Python implementations all agreed on it

macros.name: EPSILON
macros.justification: Modernize=false definition. NOTE: the default Modernize=true swaps it to \delta (line 343); kept as \epsilon because all three implementations agreed on it

macros.name: arcsec
macros.justification: Hardy maps it to \ArcSec = \DeclareMathOperator{arc\,sec}; KaTeX has no \DeclareMathOperator so the upright run \operatorname is used (all three implementations agreed)

macros.name: arccsc
macros.justification: Hardy maps it to \ArcSec = \DeclareMathOperator{arc\,sec}; KaTeX has no \DeclareMathOperator so the upright run \operatorname is used (all three implementations agreed)

macros.name: arccot
macros.justification: Hardy maps it to \ArcSec = \DeclareMathOperator{arc\,sec}; KaTeX has no \DeclareMathOperator so the upright run \operatorname is used (all three implementations agreed)

macros.name: sech
macros.justification: Standard operator absent from KaTeX's default table; no corpus preamble

macros.name: csch
macros.justification: Standard operator absent from KaTeX's default table; no corpus preamble

macros.name: cotan
macros.justification: Alias for \cot in older transcriptions; no corpus preamble

macros.name: Sum

macros.name: Prod
macros.justification: No corpus preamble defines it; a classical-transcription convention kept for the DP/PG texts.

macros.name: Lim
macros.justification: No corpus preamble defines it; a classical-transcription convention kept for the DP/PG texts.

macros.name: Log
macros.justification: A capitalized operator marks a principal value (Hardy's Log), so it stays capitalized and upright rather than folding into \log

macros.justification: Capitalized principal-value arc function, rendered as 'arc sin' etc.

macros.name: Arccos
macros.justification: Capitalized principal-value arc function, rendered as 'arc sin' etc.

macros.name: Arctan
macros.justification: Capitalized principal-value arc function, rendered as 'arc sin' etc.

macros.name: DPtypo
macros.justification: \newcommand{\DPtypo}[2]{#2}: keeps the second (corrected) argument

macros.name: DPchg
macros.justification: \newcommand{\DPchg}[2]{#2}: keeps the second (corrected) argument. Hardy's Modernize=false variant keeps #1; the default is Modernize=true

macros.name: DPmod
macros.justification: \newcommand{\DPmod}[2]{#2}: keeps the second (corrected) argument. Hardy's Modernize=false variant keeps #1; the default is Modernize=true

macros.name: Typo
macros.justification: \newcommand{\Typo}[2]{#2}

macros.name: Chg
macros.justification: \newcommand{\Chg}[2]{#2}

macros.name: Add
macros.justification: Added text is kept: \Add{#1} is #1 (Hardy Modernize=true) or \Chg{}{#1} / \DPtypo{}{#1}

macros.name: DPnote
macros.justification: \newcommand{\DPnote}[1]{}: a transcriber's note that never renders

macros.name: DPPageSep
macros.justification: \DPPageSep{scan}{page} only emits a page label

macros.name: PageSep
macros.justification: \newcommand{\PageSep}[1]{\ignorespaces}: page-break marker

macros.name: Pagelabel
macros.justification: Defines a \label only; the optional [type] argument cannot be expressed as a text macro, so ratex does not register it

macros.name: PageLabel
macros.justification: Defines a \label only; has an optional argument (see Pagelabel)

macros.name: DPlabel
macros.justification: Anchor and \label only; renders nothing

macros.name: ResetCols
macros.justification: Resets the column count; renders nothing and takes an optional argument

macros.name: First
macros.justification: \newcommand{\First}[1]{\textsc{#1}}; text-only normalizers keep just the argument

macros.name: Inum
macros.justification: \newcommand{\Inum}[1]{{\upshape#1}}; text-only normalizers keep just the argument
